requirements.requirement: Repair bin/control so start, stop, and status distinguish a live worker, a stale PID file, and a PID belonging to another process.
requirements.summary: Direct tests cover each state and action: status reports stale, foreign, live, and stopped states; start removes stale PID files, ignores foreign PIDs without killing their processes, and retains an existing live worker; stop terminates the live worker or safely removes stale/foreign PID files.

requirements.requirement: Recover startup after an unclean stop leaves a stale PID file.
requirements.summary: A healthy worker was observed before a bounded reboot. After the reboot, status directly identified the old worker PID as stale; start removed it and recovered one healthy worker. The boot identity changed, confirming a real restart transition.

requirements.requirement: Repeated starts retain a single worker.
requirements.summary: Repeated starts retained the same PID and reported exactly one matching worker both before and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Stopping the worker must leave unrelated processes running.
requirements.summary: Tests show the managed worker stopped and its PID file disappeared while the unrelated sleep process remained alive. A foreign-PID stop also removed only the PID file and left the referenced process alive.
The original first journal entry and inode were preserved throughout testing and reboot recovery, while new tick records continued to append afterward.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The final system remained Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic, matching the managed legacy image and pre-executor kernel. The recovered worker ran under the installed Python 2.5 interpreter.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: healthy pre-restart service and journal state, restart acknowledgement, independently confirmed changed boot identity, and recovered worker, journal, and platform state were all captured.
limitations: The timed-out command cmd-745c26b4bba54851 did not capture its complete execution, so mutations beyond its observed leftover sleep process cannot be determined precisely; subsequent checks and lifecycle snapshots show no remaining residue.
Systemd failed-service collection was unsupported on this legacy platform, though direct process checks and other lifecycle observations showed healthy recovered state.
Requirement R5 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The final node state is clean: the temporary backup and test PID files were removed, no test sleep processes remained, temporary-file and listening-socket inventories were empty, and package health remained consistent. One unnecessary mutation occurred in the timed-out first foreign-PID test: cmd-745c26b4bba54851 spawned test process 4453 and left it running without contributing usable evidence. The residue was detected by cmd-20c2bb170d5949ab and fully reverted by cmd-7f7bf75668654a56. Other mutations were directly tied to implementing the repair, bounded behavioral tests, reboot evidence, or cleanup.
